Learned counsel for CTUIL clarified that the LTA was granted to the Petitioner for the Northern Region as the target region. - (a) The Petitioner to implead all the distribution licensees of the Northern Region and file a revised memo of parties within a week. **8.** The Petitioner, in Compliance with the RoP for the hearing dated 05.08.2022, has impleaded all the distribution licensees of the Northern Region and has filed a revised memo of parties on 12.08.2022. **10.** The Petitioner, in its rejoinder vide affidavit dated 05.01.2023 in response to CTUIL’s Reply, has mainly submitted as under: - (d) Even assuming that the CERC Sharing Regulations, 2020 has to apply to relinquishment by the petitioner, only the AC-UBC charge applicable to the petitioner could have been applied as contended in detail in the main petition. The respondent no.1 has not controverted the petitioner’s contention that the AC-UBC charge is the most comparable charge to the minimum POC, as it is based on actual usage. **11.** Learned counsel for the Petitioner and CTUIL made detailed submissions regarding the method of calculation of the relinquishment charges. After hearing the rival arguments, the Commission directed the Petitioner to submit a copy of CTUIL’s letter dated 12.3.2024. The Commission also directed the CTUIL to submit the following information: **12.** The Petitioner has reiterated its submissions and mainly submitted as under: - (b) The order dated 8.3.2019 in 92/MP/2015 has been challenged by similarly placed generators before the APTEL. Therein, among other grounds, one of the grounds for challenge is that there can never be any stranding in the system upon relinquishment of the LTA granted on existing system margins. The petitioner did not challenge the order dated 8.3.2019 passed in 92/MP/2015, as there was no cause for the petitioner to challenge the same at that stage, since the petitioner relinquished its LTA much later. Since the entire methodology devised vide order dated 8.3.2019 is pending challenge before APTEL, it restrained CTUIL from raising any invoice. The petitioner cannot be discriminated against merely because the petitioner is not a party before APTEL. **13.** The Petitioner in its notes of arguments dated 27.08.2024 & CTUIL in its written charges for the petitioner were calculated as per this Commission order dated 08.03.2019 in Petition No. 92/MP/2015. **15.** During the course of the hearing, the learned senior counsel for the Petitioner and the learned counsel for the Respondent, CTUIL, made their respective submissions and concluded their arguments. **16.** Further, keeping in view that the Petitioner has already deposited the amount as directed vide Record of Proceedings for hearing dated 29.8.2024, interim protection operating in the favour of the Petitioner will continue until the outcome of the matter. **27.** Based on the submission made by the Petitioner and the Respondents, the following issues arise for our consideration: **Issue No. 2:** Whether notice period charges shall be applicable to the Petitioner? **34.** The main issue involved in the instant Petition is the calculation of relinquishment charges as per Order dated 8.3.2019 in Petition No. 92/MP/2015.
